label: D1 after an unrewarded trial (no-reward input), stronger when the agent leans toward a1
explanation: Fires only at D1, and only when the previous trial went unrewarded (in_rew == 0). It never fires at GO or D2, or after a rewarded trial. The predicate catches essentially every activation (dev recall 1.00, mass recall 1.00), but only about 53% of unrewarded D1 steps are active (F1 0.70). Magnitude and firing both depend on the policy direction at that D1: all top-half activations fall on steps where the a1-minus-a2 logit is above -1.5. Activations peak when the agent is about to pick a1 (top windows are mostly good=S1 with a1 chosen). The feature is nearly silent when the policy strongly favors a2 (logit below -4.4). Adding choice > -1.52 raises precision to 0.65 but drops F1 to 0.68, and adding upcoming action == 1 gives precision 0.69 and F1 0.63, so I recorded the simpler observed predicate. Previous transition type and the outcome two trials back did not separate active from inactive cases. The feature also never fires when value is above 8.1. So this is a no-reward-at-D1 detector gated by an a1-leaning or uncertain policy.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=D1 & last=a2 S2 u (+8.14), phase=D1 & last=a1 S2 u (+5.34), phase=D1 (+4.79), phase=D1 & value_bin=decile 7 (9 = highest) (+2.08), phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 8 (9 = most a1) (+1.89), phase=D1 & value_bin=decile 0 (9 = highest) (+1.81). Lower it: in_rew=1 (-10.50), ep_bucket=0 (-5.08), prev_state=1 (-4.55), phase=GO (-4.20).
